extracted.intended_audience: Support Directorate / DD/S staff responsible for OMB Circular A-44 compliance, reports management, and records/information processing
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and coordinating Directorate/Staff inputs and programs in response to OMB Circular A-44 (Management Improvement Program), including reports management, cost-reduction reporting, information-processing project proposals, and records microfilming pilot evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report scope limitation (staff-only budget)
rubrics_metrics.description: In limiting our report to our own Staff budget (which/is primarily personnel costs) and programs under our managerial control, our only input to the Management Improvement Program can be by rendering staff assistance on Agency and Directorate wide programs (i.e. Reports Management Program which is a part of OMB Circular A-44).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing the A-44 response, restrict the report to items within the Staff's own budget and managerial control; contributions beyond that must be framed as staff assistance to Agency/Directorate-wide programs (e.g., coordination roles, proposal development).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate DD/S Reports Management Program
rubrics_metrics.description: This we are doing by coordinating the DD/S Reports Management Program and developing new concepts and proposals for managing Information Processing activities in the Support Directorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Staff's role includes coordinating the Directorate's reports management efforts, assessing centrally prepared management information reports, and developing new concepts for information processing as part of fulfilling A-44 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess value and need for centrally prepared management information reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The Support Directorate has responsibility for assessing the value and need for regulatory and other centrally prepared management information reports produced by or for offices of the Support Directorate and disseminated throughout the Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform an inventory and review of management reports to determine whether each report is needed or provides sufficient value to justify its cost and continued production/distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports inventory and cost accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: A reports inventory has been completed identifying 1600 management information reports in the DDS, and with an overall cost of $1,636,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a complete inventory listing reports, counts, and associated costs as the basis for cost-reduction planning and quota assignments required by OMB Circular A-44 transmittal instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-reduction target and quota assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost reduction goal for FY 1972 established by O/PPB for the Support Directorate is a 7.5% reduction of approximately $125,000. Quotas have been assigned to various Support Offices and Support Services Staff will provide assistance in developing a continuing reports management program to meet these goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the centrally established percentage reduction target to the inventory/cost baseline, allocate quotas to subordinate offices, and supply programmatic and technical assistance to meet assigned reduction goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Processing project development and tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: The Information Processing Branch of SSS continues its work in design, testing and implementation of various information processing system areas. At present, there are ten major systems under design and these major systems are further subdivided into 41 subsystems or projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and track major systems and subsystems (design, test, implementation phases); include proposals for new approaches to information processing in annual program submissions and coordinate those proposals with Directorate planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey and selection criteria for microform/microfilming applications
rubrics_metrics.description: There have been studies and much discussion about the development of a program for microfilming Agency records as a means of getting some relief for critical space problems... there is a consensus among experts in the field that microfilming cannot normally be justified for the primary purpose of conserving space. Nevertheless, a recently completed study suggests that it may be cost effective to microfilm certain collections of records for the primary purpose of conserving storage space, provided that certain criteria can be met in the collection of files to microfilm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before committing to microfilming, identify and apply pre-established selection criteria to record collections (e.g., suitability, access patterns, cost-effectiveness). Conduct detailed cost–benefit analyses on carefully selected candidate collections to determine if microfilming is justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost–benefit analysis and feasibility review for microfilming pilots
rubrics_metrics.description: We are now undertaking a detailed cost benefit analysis of a few carefully selected of records. This analysis involves the identification of record collections in Support Directorate offices which meet as many as possible of the pre-established criteria. Representatives of the Support Services Staff and the Printing Services Division, OL, will review information collected in this survey in terms of broader system implications as well as the feasibility of treating them as individual applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct detailed cost–benefit studies; have SSS and Printing Services review results for system-level implications and feasibility; develop additional data as required prior to pilot selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement microfilming pilot projects on selected collections
rubrics_metrics.description: We expect to mount two or three pilot filming projects within the next six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select 2–3 pilot projects from collections that pass the criteria and cost–benefit review; use pilots to evaluate practical implications and inform broader program decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide staff assistance in developing continuing reports management program
rubrics_metrics.description: Support Services Staff will provide assistance in developing a continuing reports management program to meet these goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond inventories and quotas, the Staff is expected to offer ongoing program development support (procedures, tools, coordination) to sustain reports management and meet OMB-mandated reductions.
